newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. says Congress clears way to protect forest.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. says Congress clears way to protect forest.

text.p: New York state Gov. George Pataki, who has been stressing his environmental record, on Thursday said Congress had cleared the way for the state and New Jersey to protect a 17,500 forest located on their border.
The land, which is located 35 miles northwest of Manhattan was threatened by a planned 13,000-unit development that now will not go forward, said Mike McKeon, a spokesman for the governor.

While all of the land to be bought lies in New York, which he said this was its single largest purchase for a state park, the pact also will help protect New Jersey's watershed, as the forest supplies water for 25 percent of its population.

"It is a remarkable piece of woodland, a watershed for milions and an outdoor recreational area accessible to 26 million people. There isn't a more deserving piece of land for protection in our state today," said Pataki, in prepared remarks.

The two states each promised to spend $10 million to pay for buying the land, while the bill that Congress approved includes $17.5 million of funding. Private sources are expected to help provide the rest of the money that will be needed to buy the land, McKeon said, adding its final price still is being negotiated, McKeon said.

Under the agreement, Sterling Forest Corp of Tuxedo, New York, will continue to own about 2,220 acres of the forest. Part of that will be preserved as open space and any further development will have to be approved by the towns of Tuxedo and Warwick, and the state Department of Environmental Conservation.
